stimulus.text: The figure shows a circle with center \(O\) and radius 6. The central angle intercepting arc \(ABC\) measures \(60^\circ\).

stem: What is the length of arc ABC?
rationale: Arc length is the fraction of the circumference cut off by the central angle: the full circumference is \(2\pi r = 2\pi(6) = 12\pi\), and the \(60^\circ\) angle is \(\frac{60}{360} = \frac{1}{6}\) of the circle, so the arc length is \(\frac{1}{6} \times 12\pi = 2\pi\). Choice A, \(12\pi\), is the FULL circumference — the student computed \(2\pi r\) but never applied the \(\frac{60}{360}\) fraction. Choice B, \(4\pi\), comes from doubling the radius to 12 (treating 6 as a diameter and 'correcting' it the wrong way) before applying the fraction: \(\frac{1}{6} \times 2\pi(12) = 4\pi\). Choice D, \(72\pi\), applies the angle fraction upside down, multiplying by \(\frac{360}{60} = 6\) instead of \(\frac{60}{360}\): \(6 \times 12\pi = 72\pi\). A useful sanity check: the arc must be shorter than the full circumference \(12\pi\), which only \(2\pi\) and \(4\pi\) satisfy, and only \(2\pi\) uses the radius as drawn.
